observations.why_probe5_missed_it: in the latch run the PWM fall at 226.59 us shows q falling with rst 0 V, cmp 3.3 V, ocpb 3.3 V and trip max 0.021 V. The saved points are 1.3 ns apart there, and the pulse is shorter
observations.trip_chain_typical: first PWM fall in the dense run, 226.6237 us, I(L) 0.5659 A. Crossings of 1.65 V relative to the PWM fall: ocp_sense raw rises -0.714 ns (I(L) 0.5652 A), trn falls -0.638, trip rises -0.572, ocpb falls -0.514, rst rises -0.395, q falls -0.238, pwm falls -0.037. trip falls +0.185 ns, so the pulse is about 0.76 ns wide and self-clears when the high side turns off
observations.blanking: bld goes high about 35 ns after the PWM rise (226.385 us rise, bld high by 226.419 us), so the trip is not blanked near the end of a 0.55 us on-time
observations.ff_corner: ff / 5.0 V / 27 C / 3.6 ohm: Vout 1.777 V mean over 280-300 us; I(L) at 117 PWM falls over 240-300 us is 0.612-0.613 A in steady cycles (min 0.496, mean 0.600 over all falls); vc-gnd_d 1.50 V against ramp 1.45 V at the falls. Whether the ff on-time is ended by the trip or by the loop was not determined (trip/rst nets not saved)

diagnosis: DESIGN DEFECT AT TYPICAL (R16). At typical / 5.0 V / 27 C the ocp_sense comparator trips at an inductor current of about 0.565 A, through raw -> trn -> trip -> ocpb -> rst -> q -> pwm, ending every on-time from ~100 us. R16 requires no trip below 0.70 A (target min). The probe5 inference (a fixed ~0.563 A peak termination) is confirmed as the current-limit path. This accounts for the 6 percent Vout shortfall at 3.6 ohm and the vc windup. Spec rows unchanged; decision record 0005 raised.
